p4.h: Applications — Protecting Equipment from Voltage Sags
p4.lead: A voltage sag is a power-quality event in which the grid voltage momentarily drops below its normal range. Most last under a second — but precision equipment stops in that instant. TSP® fills that instant, right in front of the equipment. <small>IEEE 1159: RMS voltage at 10–90% of nominal for half a cycle to one minute</small>
p4.s1: How a sag stops a line
p4.li1: Equipment stops → hours to days to restart and requalify
p4.li2: Wafers, panels and cells in process are mostly scrapped
p4.li3: UPS covers only part of the plant, limited by capacity and cost
p4.note: ※ The benefit is greatest where a process must «start over once stopped» — vacuum, temperature and gas sequences.
p4.band: Not an outage, so not in the statistics — yet it stops the line more often than one
pl.lead: Sags happen regardless of what a customer does. The moment a tool stops, the loss does not end with one product — it spreads through five stages.
pl.c1s: Wafers, panels and cells in process are mostly scrapped
pl.c2s: Hard stops, broken vacuum and heater drift damage the tool itself
pl.c3s: Restart and re-qualification take hours to days while the line sits idle
pl.c4s: Process spread widens right after restart and latent defects follow
pl.c5s: Late deliveries and quality issues erode customer trust
pl.s1: Why sags cost more than outages
pl.l1: Even without an outage, voltage drops for ~300 ms while protection relays isolate the fault — and the tool stops in that gap
pl.l2: Outages happen 0–1 times a year; sags happen dozens of times — and the tool stops every time
pl.l3: 94.5% of sags end within 1 second (EPRI DPQ) — ride through that second and most of the loss is avoided
pl.l4: UPS covers only a few tools because of capacity and cost — the line stops at its weakest tool
pl.r1: Natural events — lightning, typhoons, heavy rain, snow, wildfires
pl.r2: Grid faults and reclosing — while the faulted section is isolated, voltage on healthy sections drops too
pl.r3: Faults at neighbouring customers and start-up of large loads travel along the same grid
pl.r4: Over within a second, so never counted as an outage — only the tool stops, and the cause is outside the plant
pl.band: One tool stops, but the whole line pays for it
ps.h: Sag Immunity Written into Equipment Specifications
ps.lead: Major semiconductor, display and battery makers write sag immunity into their common equipment specifications. Tool makers supply their equipment on the condition that it meets this requirement.
ps.tspl2: Up to 1 s at 0 % residual (100 % outage) — spec met
ps.pvl: Spec limit: 1 s · 100 % outage (dot at lower right)
ps.okl: Samsung spec — any sag in this area must be ridden through
ps.xl: Duration (s) — how long the sag lasts
ps.yl: Residual voltage (% of nominal) · 0 = full outage
ps.svgnote: Y-axis: residual voltage vs. nominal (0 % = full outage); X-axis: duration. Any sag above the curve must not stop the tool. Samsung’s POWER Vaccine spec requires ride-through of a 1-second 100 % outage — TSP® covers this entire region and meets the spec.
ps.p1s: "Equipment shall maintain normal operation under the sag depth and duration conditions defined in SEMI F47 and similar voltage-sag standards" — a common condition of equipment procurement
ps.p2s: Built on SEMI F47 · IEC 61000-4-11 · ITIC, Samsung and others require immunity to a full 1-second interruption
ps.p2: In-house specs stricter than the standards
ps.p4s: A TSP® in front of the tool meets the 1-second · 100 % outage spec (up to 3 s ride-through) — Smart POWER Vaccine® · SEMI F47 evaluation report on file
ps.p4: The answer — TSP® built in or mounted
ps.band: The spec asks for one thing — "do not stop" — and TSP® writes it into the tool

p6.lead: In normal operation the SCR static switch passes utility power straight through while TSP® stands by (off-line). The instant a sag is detected, the SCR opens and energy stored in the EDLC (ultracapacitor) feeds the load through the inverter and transformer within 2ms. When compensation ends, TSP® returns to standby.
p6.svgnote: Normal: SCR on (bypass)  ·  Sag: SCR off → EDLC · inverter · TR feed the load
p6.p2s: EDLC capacitors · 10+ years, no replacement · lower fire risk than battery-based systems
p6.p3s: Bypass in normal use · no noise, dust or fan failure
p6.p4s: Line-by-line adoption, no electrical room rework
p6.p5s: Sag-VIEWER™ — time, voltage and duration logged as data
p6.band: Invisible at 98% every day, 2ms at the critical moment — the two faces of compensation
pu.h: TSP® and UPS — Two Kinds of Power Protection with Different Purposes
pu.lead: First-time readers usually ask, “Why not just use a UPS?” The two are not competitors; they serve different purposes — a UPS for long outages, TSP® for voltage sags on production equipment.
pu.r1a: Ride through voltage sags — dips lasting from half a cycle to a few seconds
pu.r1b: Keep the load running through an outage (backup) · power conditioning
pu.r2a: Utility power passes straight through (SCR bypass) — 98% efficiency
pu.r2b: Typically continuous power conversion (on-line type) — conversion losses at all times
pu.r5a: Up to 2,400 kVA per line or incoming supply — smaller footprint, lower cost
pu.r5b: Batteries, floor space and cost rise steeply with capacity
pu.r6a: No batteries — 10+ years without replacement · no cooling fan (≤ 50 kVA)
pu.r6b: Battery life management and periodic replacement required
pu.mixd: The two do not replace each other. Servers and control systems that need outage backup take a UPS; precision tools on the line take TSP®. In plants that already run a UPS, TSP® protects the rest of the equipment the UPS does not cover.
pu.band: UPS for long outages, TSP® for voltage sags — different purposes, so together they complement each other
pc.h: Individual and Central Compensation — Two Answers from One Full Line-up
pc.lead: Only WESCO in Korea covers single-phase 0.5 kVA to three-phase 2,400 kVA under one brand. That is why we can propose protecting tools one by one, protecting a whole line with one unit, or a mix — to fit the site.
pc.a1: Single-phase 0.5–20 kVA · three-phase 5–200 kVA — sized to each tool
pc.a2: 2 ms transfer · 1–3 s compensation; can be built into or mounted on the tool (Smart POWER Vaccine®)
pc.a3: Start with critical tools, no electrical-room work — suits existing lines and tool-spec compliance
pc.b: Central compensation — per line or plant
pc.b1: One three-phase 300–2,400 kVA unit on the secondary of the line's main panel protects the whole line
pc.b2: 4 ms transfer · 3 s compensation standard; no changes on the tool side
pc.b3: Suits new lines, FABs and plants with many tools — one large unit simplifies investment and maintenance
pc.mixd: The two are combined by tool count, electrical-room space and investment stage: critical tools individually, the line centrally — designed within one brand, so monitoring (Sag-VIEWER™) stays unified as well.
pc.band: One at a time or all at once — only a wide line-up lets you pick the right answer for the site
p7.h: Sag-VIEWER™ — This is what you see on the panel
p7.lead: The 7-inch touch panel shows live measurements alongside the event record. Tap a menu.
p7.c1: Input and output voltage, current, DC charge level, detection and recovery thresholds — on one screen.
p7.c2: The grid waveform at the moment of the sag (top) and the load waveform TSP produced (bottom), side by side — with the time, voltage and duration recorded.
p7.c3: Up to 500 records — breaker operations, start and stop, setting changes.
p7.c4: Apparent, active and reactive power plus cumulative energy — by hour, day, month or year.
p7.c5: Detection level, recovery hysteresis and compensation time — adjustable on site.
p7.band: Every event becomes data — compensation log, waveforms and energy on one screen
